messages:
incident-bot: Paging: spike in inference 5xx and model-variant mismatches reported by canaries. Affected regions: eu-central-1, ap-southeast-1. Suspected cause: DNS partial propagation + fallback policy prioritizing region fallback. Pager delivered to @sre-oncall-sam.

sre-oncall-sam: I'm on it. initial telemetry: heavy retry loops between eu and ap nodes, long tail latencies, and some responses truncated. traces show alternate IPs for same VIP depending on resolver.

neteng-anya: I'm seeing inconsistent A records across resolvers for gateway.edge.redwood.example. TTL was 300s but several enterprise resolvers still returning old A records. Ran these checks:
```
# sample queries
dig @8.8.8.8 gateway.edge.redwood.example A +short
# 52.23.45.1

dig @203.0.113.5 gateway.edge.redwood.example A +short
# 10.250.3.12
```

ml-runtime-lee: that 10.250.x IP range is from an older cluster where quantized-v1-small lived. If traffic bounces there we'll see semantic regressions. Our routing policy currently falls back across regions when a node is unhealthy; that could trigger variant mismatch.

support-jasmin: customers reporting: slower responses and "answers are garbled; feels like different model". Logged 9 customer incidents so far, main impact on embedding and chat endpoints.

product-nick: flagging customer-facing clarity: avoid implying data exposure. say: "service degradation due to routing and DNS propagation; results may be lower-quality."

sre-oncall-sam: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily set routing fallback to prefer local variant downgrade over cross-region route 2) cancel any pending global DNS changes we pushed 3) request CDN edge flush 4) escalate to registrar if glue records stale 5) monitor for oscillation. Executing step 1 now.

incident-bot: command executed by sre-oncall-sam at 1845694440: 
`rwctl routing update --fallback-order model_variant,local_instance,region`

ml-runtime-lee: pushing config change to alias maps so alias 'prod-llm' resolves to local smaller variant instead of cross-region alias. rolling to eu first.

neteng-anya: CDN ticket open (#CDN-4890). Pushed purge to POPs with highest affected metrics. Also lowered edge TTL to 60s. Noted that some corporate resolvers have internal caching beyond TTL.

support-jasmin: sending interim message to affected customers: "We're actively mitigating a routing/DNS issue causing degraded inference; we expect progressive recovery as DNS caches clear. We'll update in 20 minutes."

sre-oncall-sam: after fallback change, 5xx dropped ~40% in eu-central within 4m. However, overall p95 latency still elevated; traces show retries hitting legacy 10.250.3.12 occasionally.

ml-runtime-lee: starting canary alias patch in eu-central at 1845694700.

incident-bot: canary started by ml-runtime-lee.

neteng-anya: ran a targeted BGP withdraw on the old cluster IPs from a few POPs to prevent accidental routing there while registrars and CDN finish purge. This is risky but should stop oscillation.

sre-oncall-sam: acknowledge the BGP change. Monitoring for collateral.

support-jasmin: updated customers: noted partial recovery; gave workaround for critical customers: force endpoint to region-specific hostname (eu.gateway.redwood.example) if possible. Provided contact for dedicated assistance.

product-nick: request adding a clear runbook item: if DNS change coincides with routing policy flips, prefer conservative fallback. We'll include that in postmortem.

ml-runtime-lee: canary shows no quality regressions. proceeding with rollout to ap-southeast next.

neteng-anya: CDN reports purge complete for 80% of POPs at 1845696000. Still seeing stale returns from a few enterprise resolvers; advised those customers to flush caches where feasible. Requested registrar support for stale glue.

sre-oncall-sam: metrics trending down. 5xx at baseline in eu-central and ap-southeast for most flows; a few long-tail resolvers still create isolated spikes. I'll keep smart-routing fallback restricted until DNS fully converges.

support-jasmin: logged all affected customer contacts and assigned follow-ups. Noting dedicated instances mostly unaffected. Shared instance customers saw more quality drift.

incident-bot: remediation actions recorded.

product-nick: creating action items: (A) enforce fallback order in default policy, (B) add DNS-propagation check before mass routing changes, (C) improve canary to detect model-variant mismatch. Assigning owners.

ml-runtime-lee: opening PR for detection: add a semantic-similarity canary between primary and fallback model to catch variant regressions during rollouts.

neteng-anya: will create a small script to query multiple public resolvers and flag divergent RRsets before rolling DNS.

sre-oncall-sam: incident state: mitigated at 1845697100. leaving open for postmortem and follow-ups. Handoff: daytime SRE to monitor for 2 hours, keep fallback override active until neteng confirms global DNS convergence.

support-jasmin: sending final customer note: "We have mitigations in place and most customers are recovering. We will follow up with support if you still see issues; credits will be assessed case-by-case."

product-nick: adding compliance tag and scheduling postmortem meeting.

incident-bot: thread archived and participants logged.
